chunks: Whoever visits a patient, seventy thousand angels accompany him seeking forgiveness for him until he returns to his house.

key_terms.شَيَّعَهُ: accompanied him, escorted him — used for the act of accompanying someone departing
key_terms.عَادَ: visited (the sick) — from 'iyada, the practice of visiting the ill
key_terms.يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ: seeking forgiveness — making istighfar (intercession for forgiveness) on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting a sick person in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the immense spiritual reward for visiting the sick, promising that seventy thousand angels will accompany the visitor and pray for his forgiveness throughout his journey home. The act of visiting the sick (Arabic: 'iyada) was considered a fundamental communal and religious duty in early Islamic society, and this narration uses the imagery of angelic intercession to underscore its elevated status. The audience — the Imam's close companions — would have understood angelic accompaniment as a concrete sign of divine pleasure and a means of gaining abundant mercy.
